newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PM asks lower house for confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: Czech PM asks lower house for confidence vote.

text.p: Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus asked the lower house of Czech parliament on Tuesday for a vote of confidence in his government and its economic programme, beginning a debate which is expected to lead to a knife-edged result.

"Our short-term aim is to stabilise the Czech economy and start to decrease the external imbalances and on that basis begin to renew the confidence of ours and the foreign public in our economy and our currency," Klaus told parliament.
He was referring to a recent sharp drop in the Czech crown which coincided with an economic slowdown and falling poplarity of the three-party centre-right coalition government.

On May 28 coalition parties agreed to an austerity package of budget cuts, public sector wage freezes and other measures aimed at stemming a widening current account deficit. Klaus said the measures would cut potentially 20 billion crowns in spending and social transfers from the 1997 budget.
The ruling coalition is expected to control 100 votes in the 200-seat house for the confidence vote which requires a simple majority of those voting for approval.

Analysts expect at least 97 opposition deputies to vote against the government, but the votes of two unaffiliated deputies are not clear and one deputy from the Communist party has said he is unable to vote for health reasons.
